Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, appreciate it. quick roll call - we'll go through scope and then Ethan will dig into benchmarks and scoring.
[00:14] Lena: Hey, Lena here. excited to get this moving.
[00:18] Rajiv: Rajiv, product. we've got some timeline pressure Q3-ish so trying to move fast.
[00:24] Sofie: Sofie on infra side, i'll handle network and security questions.
[00:27] Ethan: Ethan, SE at Redwood. i'll cover performance and the eval plan.
[00:31] Maya: Great, thanks. high-level ask from Axiom as i understand: embed LLM responses into retail analytics workflow, need high precision entity extraction and a chat assistant that keeps hallucination under control and outputs strict JSON. is that right, Lena?
[00:45] Lena: Yes exactly. our main slas are about accuracy on product normalization and basically zero bad JSON.
[00:52] Maya: Cool. i'll quickly go over the proposed success criteria, shout if i'm off.
[00:56] Maya: Proposed success criteria: 1) latency p95 < 350ms for short chat turns, 2) throughput 100 concurrent reqs (sustained), 3) hallucination rate < 2% on golden set, 4) JSON schema conformance 99%, and 5) qualitative score on golden prompts >= 0.85 (we'll define scoring).
[01:18] Rajiv: 350ms p95 is fine but can we get a comparison to current infra? right now our homegrown model is around 200-500ms depending on load. 
[01:29] Ethan: Yeah we can run apples-to-apples. we'll execute the benchmark on our Dedicated sim and also do a hosted run if you want. note: kernel selection and quantization will affect 350 target, we'll call out model variant.
[01:41] Lena: The hallucination metric is critical - can you explain how you define a hallucination? we've seen fuzzy product names that are wrong but look plausible.
[01:50] Ethan: Good question. for this pilot we propose a two-tier approach: automated detection via entity-matching (semantic similarity threshold + product catalog lookup) plus manual review on a sample. automated flagging will mark anything that doesn't match catalog above 0.85 similarity as potential hallucination. then human review on the goldset to compute final hallucination rate.
[02:09] Maya: Also we'll include format checks - enforce JSON schema, reject outputs that don't validate. we can run a strict parser as part of the pipeline.
[02:17] Sofie: for secure data flow, can you confirm logs won't include PII and we'll be able to disable token retention? we need that for compliance.
[02:25] Maya: yes, we have a private deployment option and controls: token redaction, no long-term retention, and KMS integrations. i'll attach the security one-pager.
[02:33] Sofie: ok please send that.
[02:36] [00:03:40] Speaker 1: (in background) right
[02:38] Ethan: zooming into the eval plan. we typically split tests into Golden Set, Regression Suite, and Load Benchmarks.
[02:45] Ethan: Golden Set: small curated set of canonical prompts (we recommend 100 but we'll accept 20 seed cases from you). golden set is used for pass/fail per-prompt and for hallucination percentage.
[02:55] Rajiv: 100 seems high, but we can do 20 to start and then expand. we have 20 'must pass' cases.
[03:02] Ethan: Perfect. Regression Suite: larger corpus of ~200-500 examples representing edge cases, format variants, and longer conversations. this is for measuring durability across model updates.
[03:14] Lena: can you explain scoring? like how do you combine semantic similarity and structural correctness?
[03:19] Ethan: Score is a weighted metric. structural pass (JSON valid) is binary and gets heavy weight (40%). semantic similarity (embedding cosine to human reference or ground truth) normalized to 0-1 gets 40%. hallucination penalty is applied - if flagged, subtract 0.5 from that example or mark fail depending on severity. final normalized score threshold 0.85 for acceptance.
[03:42] Maya: We also include a human review rubric for a sample of N=50 examples to calibrate the automated scorer.
[03:49] Lena: ok that feels reasonable. what about format variants? we often have multiple currencies and SKU formats that confuse parsers.
[03:57] Ethan: we'll add format checkers with regex and schema variations; the regression suite should include currency edge cases. we'll also add a post-processing step that maps sku aliases to canonical ids using your catalog.
[04:08] [00:06:20] Speaker 2: oh yeah
[04:09] Rajiv: On workload sizing — here's what we expect: avg prompt length ~120 tokens, 75% single-turn queries, 25% multi-turn follow-ups, expected peak of 150 rps during reporting window, steady-state 30 rps.
[04:23] Ethan: Good. for benchmarks we'll simulate both steady-state and burst patterns. recommended hardware for Dedicated run: 2x A100-style nodes for the bench (we'll size after sample run).
[04:34] Sofie: we want to avoid large infra surprises — can you give an early cost estimate for the pilot testbed?
[04:39] Maya: we'll put together an estimated burn rate in the SOW. rough ballpark depends on model variant, but we'll call out per-hour cluster cost in the SOW.
[04:47] Ethan: Regarding tolerances: JSON conformance 99% stretch, but we expect some fuzzy parsing; we'll instrument prefix caching and KV cache behavior to reduce latency for conversational flows. note: kv cache sometimes transcribed as K-V cache in logs.
[05:03] Maya: let's talk timeline. we propose a 6-week pilot:
[05:07] Maya: Week 0-1: onboarding and dataset collection (you upload prompts + golden set)
[05:11] Maya: Week 2: initial benchmark run (functional + perf)
[05:14] Maya: Week 3-4: tuning, model variant runs, quantization experiments
[05:18] Maya: Week 5: regression run and human review sample
[05:20] Maya: Week 6: final acceptance and debrief, decision point
[05:24] Lena: that timeline works if we can deliver prompts by end of week 1.
[05:28] Rajiv: what are expected acceptance gates? aside from the numeric thresholds, are there business acceptances?
[05:33] Ethan: Acceptance gates: numeric thresholds (latency, throughput, hallucination, JSON pass rate), plus business sign-off on 20 golden prompts (they must be approved by product). if any gate fails we'll enter remediation with scope/timeboxed fixes.
[05:46] Lena: remediation path is important. we can't be stuck if a model just flunks.
[05:50] Maya: agreed — we'll include an auto-fallback policy in the pilot to route critical requests to a safe model variant and backfill while we patch.
[05:58] [00:09:40] Speaker 3: mm-hm
[06:00] Ethan: For hallucination checks specifically: we'll implement a) catalog lookup, b) semantic similarity threshold, c) hallucination classifier (optional). together they reduce false negatives; classifier requires labeled data but we can train on a small seed.
[06:14] Lena: we have some labeled false positives from earlier runs — we'll share those.
[06:17] Ethan: great, that'll speed up classifier tuning.
[06:20] Maya: on reporting — the console will show per-prompt traces, per-token cost, and golden-set regression dashboards. we'll share a read-only link to the benchmark workbook after runs.
[06:30] Rajiv: can you walk me through an example scoring calc?
[06:33] Ethan: yep quick example: example A: JSON valid (structural pass = 1), semantic sim = 0.92, hallucination flag = 0 => raw = 0.4*1 + 0.4*0.92 - 0 = 0.768, plus human calibration bump from sample review +0.09 => final ~0.858 -> pass. if hallucination flag true severe, we mark as fail regardless.
[06:56] Maya: We should also call out SLOs vs SLA — SLO targets for p95 latency and a separate SLA for availability will be in the SOW.
[07:04] Sofie: for private deployment we need SAML SSO, SOC2 attestation, KMS key control, and audit log forwarding — can you confirm support?
[07:12] Maya: yes to all; i'll attach compliance docs. note that SOC2 report delivery timing may affect start of private deployment.
[07:20] Lena: one more question on regression cadence — if we ship a model update during pilot, how are results compared?
[07:27] Ethan: we'll use anchored baselines — every model variant is scored against the same golden set and regression suite; we'll track delta per example and compute regression rate. automatic rollback on major regressions is possible in Dedicated.
[07:40] Rajiv: ok sounds thorough. any blockers?
[07:43] Sofie: i need the network poke instructions and a bullet list of required egress/ingress rules.
[07:49] Maya: i'll add that to the SOW.
[07:52] [00:12:45] Speaker 4: right right
[07:55] Maya: to recap quick: 1) Axiom to upload 200 prompts + seed 20 golden prompts, 2) Redwood to send SOW + bench workbook + security docs, 3) schedule initial benchmark week of 6/14, 4) pilot target 6-weeks.
[08:10] Lena: all good. send the SOW and we'll review.
[08:13] Rajiv: please include an itemized list of what happens if golden set fails.
[08:16] Ethan: will do — we'll include remediation steps and expected SLAs for fixes.
[08:20] Maya: anything else?
[08:22] Lena: no, thanks everyone. excited to get started.
[08:25] Maya: great thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts. bye all.
